Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have everything captured: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Latency SLO: FinCo is aiming for p95 end-to-end response time <= 300 ms for the primary chat flow (low-latency assistant interactions).
- Context window: typical requests will include large context (user + conversation + doc snippets). You said average input size ~4k tokens with some spikes up to 8k tokens.
- Output size: usually 256–1,024 tokens (most responses ~256).
- Concurrency/throughput: expected sustained concurrency ~50 active users with bursts up to 200 concurrent requests; peak QPS ~120.
- Streaming: must support streamed token delivery to the client (so app shows progressive tokens).
- Compliance note: all traffic must be routed via customer VPC or dedicated capacity and encrypted in transit.

Performance notes / known tradeoffs (high level):
- Longer context windows (4k -> 8k) increase memory footprint and per-request compute; this typically increases latency and reduces effective throughput unless using dedicated GPUs with larger memory + optimized kernels.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency (user sees tokens sooner) but does not remove backend generation cost; total end-to-end still depends on model steps and token counts.
- Batching is a cost saver but adds queuing latency; for strict p95 targets we commonly recommend dedicated capacity with minimal batching.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-slo-side-by-side.pdf (SLO options and recommended configs), sample-load-profile.csv (please confirm your actual QPS / payload distribution if different).

Could you confirm the two quick items so Rishi can size the technical deep-dive correctly?
1) Typical/median input tokens vs peak input tokens (you mentioned ~4k avg, 8k peak — confirm).
2) Is p95 300 ms a hard requirement for all user types, or a target for the most frequent (interactive) path only?

Next steps:
- Rishi (SE) to propose configuration options and expected latency numbers for 2k/4k/8k contexts (we’ll call out tradeoffs).
- Schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra team to go over network topology, payload samples, and QPS matrix.
- You to share network topology diagram and any compliance constraints (Priya if you can send the diagram that would be great).

Hi Alex — thanks for the detail and the topology. Quick technical summary and realistic expectations based on the numbers you provided. I’ll follow with an agenda for the deep-dive.

Short answers:
- Can we hit p95 <= 300 ms at 8k context with streaming at your target concurrency? Not with a generic shared-hosted configuration. Realistically, to hit that p95 for 8k context you will want: dedicated reserved capacity (pinned GPUs), optimized kernels (we’ll pick a quantization profile), and strict routing (no large batching). Even then, depending on model choice, p95 can be in the 300–450 ms range for interactive-length outputs (<=256 tokens) — 300 ms is achievable for many model+hardware combos but it’s tight at 8k.

Why:
- Context impact: latency grows super-linearly with sequence length because attention and KV cache management costs increase. Going from 2k -> 8k can add 2–4x CPU/GPU work per generated token depending on model.
- Streaming: streaming gives users token-by-token experience (reduced perceived latency), but backend still needs to compute earlier tokens; you’ll see first token faster if we do incremental decoding and avoid large decode batches. End-to-end for full response still follows generation cost.
- Concurrency and batching: to keep p95 low we avoid batching in the interactive path. That reduces throughput efficiency; to compensate we provision more GPUs.

Recommended configurations to evaluate (we’ll bring detailed numbers in the deep dive):
A) Dedicated + large-memory GPUs + quantized FP16/KP kernels: best for 8k context + low p95; expect p95 ~300–450 ms for typical interactive responses.
B) Dedicated + sharding across multiple GPUs (sequence-parallel): helps with very long contexts but increases infra complexity; can reduce p95 variance for extreme payloads.
C) Hybrid: use prefix caching and route long-context/low-priority requests to a lower-cost pool; keep interactive short-context requests on a low-latency pool.

Requests for the deep-dive (please provide before the call):
- sample payloads (we included sample-load-profile.csv — please populate with token distributions and payload sizes).
- expected QPS matrix by region and by user type (interactive vs batch).
- any constraints on model family (open model vs customer-supplied) and max allowed quantization.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60 minutes):
1) Review sample payloads & QPS matrix (10m)
2) Network topology & routing (10m)
3) Model/quantization options and memory/pinning tradeoffs (15m)
4) Cost vs latency tradeoffs and recommended Dedicated configs (15m)
5) Action items & next steps (10m)
